newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: U.N. Command in S.Korea protests to N.Korea.
newsitem.headline: U.N. Command in S.Korea protests to N.Korea.

text.p: The U.S.-led United Nations Command in South Korea on Thursday protested to North Korea over a shooting incident at the border on Wednesday, a command statement said.

In a protest note handed over at the border, the U.N. Command accused North Korea of violating an armistice accord that ended the 1950-53 Korean War. The North Korean side did not accept the protest, the statement said.
The protest was made through the Military Armistice Commission, which monitors the ceasefire, and was handed over at the border truce village of Panmunjom.
An investigation by the U.N. Command found North Korea "committed an Armistice Agreement violation", the statement said.
South Korea says Northern forces fired artillery and machineguns at Southern guard posts as part of a deliberate provocation that began when 14 Northern soldiers crossed the border line.
North Korea says several of its soldiers were wounded in what was one of the most serious clashes in many years along the heavily fortified border.
